title: New Orleans drummers: Henry Zeno, Red Happy, Tubby and Minor Hall
summary: Jackson recalls Henry Zeno's solos, Red Happy as the greatest drummer for execution, the Hall brothers, and the La Rocca boys' neighbourhood.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And Celestan, Celestan has always read music. Guy Kelly made read music. I know so many fellas that read music. He can't tell me that they didn't read music. And so as I was foreseeing about Celestan, that was a band I really enjoyed. The drums, the drummer, Henry Zeno, used to take a solo, or maybe about 24 bars. That's the tune that was playing. And then the drums, and then the drums, and then it falls in again.
You understand? They take the drum solo in those days then.

Yeah. And then I began to get a little larger and a little older naturally, and I go a little straight a little farther from home. And I began to see Red Happy. Now Red Happy, I'll tell you, was the greatest drummer as far as execution.
Well Lee Collins always said that.

Yeah, that ever hitting New Orleans as far as execution. I read Happy would have a lot of things to back him, over him, and everywhere, you know. And he'd make a break and hit all those different things, and coming on time he was a great drummer. I think he was even greater than Baby Dotson. Baby Bots was a good drummer, was a fine drummer, as in his prime he was still a good drummer. But Happy was supposed to have been the best. And the old man, and his first band in 1911, Cottrell. Oh yeah, the old man. Yeah, Cottrell and Zeno. Zeno and now here's Tubby Hall and Minor Hall. A relative of theirs taught me at New Orleans University. I remember seeing Tubby Hall when I was a little fellow, I only lived, they lived around Cadie Street, right by the La Rocca Boys. The La Rocca Boys, people, had a grocery store on Ferret. It was either Cadie and Ferret or Jen and Ferret. I knew that. Now those boys come on that first, what do you call them? Original Dixieland band.

That's where the La Rocca Boys come from. So Tubby Hall and his brother, Minor, I saw them playing drums when I was a kid, you understand? And they are cousins to the Humphreys. Yeah, they are cousins to the Humphreys. Yeah, so I saw Happy, then I began to see Mud Carey, Jack Carey, two brothers. Then I began to attend the dances. I'd sneak away from home and borrow somebody's pants, long pants, you know, and sometimes we'd have to saw them down to my side one way or the other, and I'd go to these dances unbeknown to my mother. She didn't know I was attending dance until the lady crossed the street. Saw me one night and told her. Then I began to see fellas, like the whole Kid Orr's band, Vigionny Dots, Orr and Mud Carey on the trumpet, Henry Zeno and fellas.
